keyEvents.event: Revolution ends the Zaydi imamate in the north; civil war draws in Egypt and Saudi Arabia
keyEvents.impact: Northern Yemen became a proxy battlefield for regional powers

keyEvents.event: Unification of North and South Yemen
keyEvents.impact: A fragile merger; the 1994 civil war left southern grievances that never healed
Six wars against the Saleh government forged a battle-hardened Zaydi revivalist movement

keyEvents.event: Arab Spring forces Ali Abdullah Saleh from power
keyEvents.impact: Failed transition opened the way for the Houthis' march on the capital
The internationally recognized government fled south, eventually to Riyadh and Aden
A decade of war and blockade produced one of the world's worst humanitarian crises but failed to dislodge the Houthis
Saudi-Houthi fighting largely stopped and back-channel talks began

keyEvents.event: Red Sea shipping campaign in support of Gaza
keyEvents.impact: Attacks on merchant ships rerouted global trade; US, UK and Israeli strikes followed but the Houthis gained regional stature

keyEvents.event: Israeli strike kills the Houthi prime minister and cabinet members; STC power grab in the south
keyEvents.impact: Leadership losses did not break the movement; the anti-Houthi camp fractured

keyEvents.event: Houthis join the Iran war, seize Mokha, Perim and the Bab al-Mandab coast, and strike Riyadh's airport
keyEvents.impact: Control of a second global chokepoint and open war with Saudi Arabia

history.narrative: Modeled as the Houthi (Ansar Allah) authority in Sanaa, which rules most of Yemen's population: a Zaydi revivalist militia-state that has outlasted Saudi bombing, US strikes and Israeli decapitation raids. Poor, besieged and ideologically fervent, it turns geography into leverage by threatening the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab.

redLines.description: Saudi-backed ground offensive on Hodeidah, Sanaa or the Red Sea coast
Assassination of Abdul-Malik al-Houthi or the senior leadership
Direct attack aimed at overthrowing the Islamic Republic, the movement's patron

internalDivisions.name: Southern secessionism and the remnants of the Southern Transitional Council
Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council forces holding Marib, Taiz and the east
Zaydi-Shafi'i sectarian divide and AQAP jihadists

goals.description: Extend control over all of Yemen, including Marib's energy fields and the southern ports
Force Saudi Arabia into a settlement that pays salaries and ends the blockade
Sustain the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab campaign as part of the axis of resistance
Emerge as the strongest surviving member of Iran's axis
